if: the inward supply is WORKS CONTRACT SERVICES supplied for CONSTRUCTION OF AN IMMOVABLE PROPERTY
AND the immovable property is NOT plant and machinery
AND the works contract service is NOT an input service for further supply of works contract service
then: input tax credit is NOT AVAILABLE on those works contract services
note: Two carve-outs, both narrow. 'Plant and machinery' carries the restricted meaning in the Explanation to s.17 — see GST-ITC-17-PM — which excludes land, buildings, other civil structures, telecommunication towers and pipelines laid outside the factory. The second carve-out saves the sub-contracting chain: a main contractor may credit a sub-contractor's works contract service, because his own output is a works contract service. 'Construction' is extended by the Explanation to clauses (c) and (d) to reach re-construction, renovation, additions, alterations and repairs, to the extent of capitalisation. Section 17(5) opens 'Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1) of section 16 and sub-section (1) of section 18', so this block defeats both the s.16(1) entitlement and the s.18(1) special-circumstances credit. Business use does not cure it. The source is the CGST Act as updated 31-08-2021. UNKNOWN whether a later amendment has changed this clause; later amendments are not held locally.
